<thought>To meet the requirement of a single‑step synthesis from commercially available precursors, I will use a cyclopropanation reaction.  
Methyl cinnamate (SMILES COC(=O)C=CC1=CC=CC=C1) is a cheap, widely stocked ester.  
Trimethylsilyl‑diazomethane (SMILES C[Si](C)(C)C=N=N) is a commercially available carbene precursor that transfers a –CH‑SiMe₃ unit onto an alkene, forming a cyclopropane bearing a trimethylsilyl substituent.  
A single‑step cyclopropanation of methyl cinnamate with trimethylsilyl‑diazomethane furnishes the target methyl ester COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O.  
Both reagents are buyable and their combined price is well under $125, satisfying the cost constraint and the ≤1‑step limit.</thought>
